brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A cold Yemeni drink made by steeping raisins, its Arabic name meaning raisin infusion. No tea leaf is involved.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: It is described as a modern adaptation of nabidh, a drink of fermented raisin sugars widely consumed in pre-Islamic Arabia that could turn mildly alcoholic if prepared for long. The non-alcoholic form is reported to have been a favourite of the Prophet Muhammad, and nabidh declined after Islam spread through the peninsula in the seventh century because of the prohibition on alcohol.
processing: Black raisins are washed thoroughly, soaked in hot water for about three hours, then pressed through a sieve-like utensil to extract the liquid. Other recipes boil the raisins or soak them overnight in the refrigerator before squeezing, and some boil them again after soaking; sugar varies with the sweetness of the raisins.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
taste_profile: A herbal infusion; the taste depends on the plant.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
